easy.def: A person who trains a team.
examples: Our coach is nice.
The coach blew the whistle.
The coach helps us.

more.def: A person who trains and teaches a team or a player.
examples: Our soccer coach teaches us how to pass.
The coach gave the team a pep talk.
She is the coach of the swim team.

easy.def: To train and teach a team.
examples: Dad coaches my team.
She coached the swimmers.
He coaches soccer.

more.def: To train and teach a person or team to get better at a sport or skill.
examples: Dad coaches my soccer team.
She coached the swimmers for the big meet.
He coaches the school chess club.

easy.def: Clothing you wear outside when it is cold.
examples: Put on your coat.
My coat is warm.
It is cold, so wear a coat.

more.def: A warm piece of clothing with sleeves that you wear over your other clothes.
examples: She zipped up her winter coat.
He hung his wet coat by the door.
A thick coat keeps you warm in the snow.

easy.def: A layer of fur or paint.
examples: The dog has a thick coat.
The wall needs a coat of paint.
Dad put on a coat of paint.

more.def: A layer of fur on an animal, or a layer of paint on a surface.
examples: The dog's thick coat keeps it warm in winter.
The wall needs two coats of paint.
A coat of snow covered the roof.

easy.def: A secret way of writing messages.
examples: We wrote in code.
The code is secret.
Can you read the code?

more.def: A set of signs, letters or numbers used to send secret messages.
examples: The spies wrote their messages in code.
We made up a code using numbers for letters.
Can you crack the code?

easy.def: Numbers that open something.
examples: The safe code is secret.

The code is on the card.

more.def: A set of numbers or letters used to open a lock or enter a place.
examples: Type the code to unlock the door.
She forgot the code to her bike lock.

easy.def: Instructions for a computer.
examples: She writes code for games.

more.def: Instructions written in a special language that tell a computer what to do.
examples: My brother writes code for video games.
A mistake in the code made the program stop.
We learned to write simple code at school.

easy.def: A hot brown drink that adults often have.
examples: Dad drinks coffee in the morning.
The coffee smells good.
Grandma has coffee with cake.

more.def: A hot, dark drink made by pouring hot water over ground, roasted beans.
examples: My aunt drinks a cup of coffee every morning before work.
The smell of fresh coffee filled the small cafe.
Coffee beans grow on trees in warm countries.

easy.def: Not warm.
examples: The ice is cold.
It is cold outside.
I want a cold drink.

more.def: Having a low temperature.
examples: The lake was too cold for swimming in April.
She wrapped her cold hands around the warm mug.
Ice cream is a cold treat on a hot day.

easy.def: A sickness that makes your nose run.

My brother caught a cold.

more.def: A mild illness that causes a runny nose, sneezing and a cough.
examples: I stayed home from school with a cold.
Wash your hands to avoid catching a cold.
A cold usually goes away after a few days.

easy.def: To bring things together.

more.def: To gather things together, sometimes as a hobby.
examples: He collects stamps from countries all around the world.
A truck collects the trash every Tuesday.
Bees collect nectar from flowers to make honey.

easy.def: A school people go to after high school.

He wants to go to college.

more.def: A school that people attend after high school to study more.
examples: My cousin is studying music at college.
Some people go to college to become teachers.
The college has a big library.

easy.def: A high officer in the army.
examples: The colonel gave orders.

A colonel stood at the gate.

more.def: A military officer of high rank, above a major and below a general.
examples: The colonel inspected the soldiers.
A colonel gave the order to move out.
The colonel wore a medal on his coat.

easy.def: Red, blue, green and so on.

more.def: Something like red, blue or yellow that you see in things.
examples: Her favorite color is purple.
The leaves change color in the fall.
The rainbow has seven colors.

easy.def: To fill in with crayons or paint.

more.def: To fill in a picture or surface with crayons, pencils or paint.
examples: I colored the picture with crayons.
She colored the sky blue.
We colored eggs in the spring.

easy.def: To move toward the one who is speaking.

My friend came to my house.

more.def: To move toward a person or place, or to arrive somewhere.
examples: Please come to the front of the class and show your drawing.
The mail carrier comes to our street every morning.
Our cousins came all the way from Texas for the holiday.

easy.def: Feeling good and soft.

more.def: Feeling relaxed and at ease, or making you feel that way.
examples: These shoes are comfortable enough to wear all day.
She felt comfortable talking to her grandmother about anything.

easy.def: To tell someone what they must do.

more.def: To give an order that must be followed.
examples: The captain commanded the crew to raise the sails.
The queen commanded her guards to open the gate.

easy.def: An order.

The captain gave a command.

more.def: An order that tells someone what to do.
examples: The dog followed the command to sit.
The captain gave the command to start.

easy.def: A person in charge of soldiers or a ship.
examples: The commander gave orders.

The commander saluted.

more.def: A person in charge of soldiers, a ship or a mission.
examples: The commander gave the order to sail.
The space commander led the crew.
The army commander met with the leaders.

easy.def: To do something wrong or bad.

more.def: To do something that is wrong or against the law.
examples: The thief committed a crime.
He committed the same mistake twice.
It is wrong to commit a crime.

easy.def: To promise to do something.

more.def: To promise to do something or to stick with it.
examples: I commit to practicing every day.
She committed to the team for the whole season.
He committed to helping with the garden.

easy.def: Seen or found often.

more.def: Found or happening often, not rare.
examples: Robins are common birds in our town.
Colds are common in the winter.
Smith is a common last name.

easy.def: The people who live in one place.

more.def: A group of people who live in the same area or who share something important.
examples: The whole community helped clean up the beach.

easy.def: A business that makes or sells things.

more.def: A business that makes or sells goods or services.

My aunt works for a company that builds bridges.
The ice cream company opened a new shop downtown.

easy.def: Visitors who are at your home.

more.def: People who come to visit, or the presence of other people with you.
examples: We are expecting company for dinner on Sunday.
The puppy kept me company while I did my homework.

examples: We compared the two maps and noticed that one had more rivers.

easy.def: To say that you are not happy.

more.def: To say that you are unhappy or upset about something.

The neighbors complained about the noise.
Please don't complain about the long walk.

easy.def: Having all its parts.

He owns a complete set of the books.

easy.def: To finish.

The runners completed the race.
He completed the puzzle in an hour.

easy.def: A machine that stores and shows information.

more.def: An electronic machine that can store information, do tasks and connect to other machines.

easy.def: A worry.

more.def: A feeling of worry about something.

easy.def: To be about something.

more.def: To be about or to involve someone or something.

easy.def: Worried.
examples: Mom was concerned.
I am concerned about the storm.
She looked concerned.

more.def: Worried about something.
examples: Mom was concerned when I was late.
We are concerned about the stray cat in the cold.
The teacher looked concerned.

easy.def: How something is.

easy.def: Weather or surroundings.

more.def: The weather or other surroundings at a time.

easy.def: To say that something is true.

easy.def: Not sure what to think.

easy.def: Words you say when someone has good news.

more.def: Words that you say to someone when something good has happened to them.

Congratulations to the graduating class!
Congratulations on your new puppy!

easy.def: To join together.

related.def: A thing that joins two things.

easy.def: To think about something carefully.
